Vivek — quick engineering assessment below. TL;DR: pilot feasible with careful sizing and a fallback plan; WebSocket fine to support and slightly better for mobile backpressure. See details/assumptions.

Assumptions
- Pilot using NVIDIA A100 (80GB) instances; model ~7B to 13B family (fp16 / int8 quantized fallback).
- Average prompt+response length assumption from Pioneer: ~350 tokens total.

TTFT expectations
- Warm model hot path: 90–140ms median TTFT for 7B-class model on A100x1 with continuous batching and KV cache warm; 120–220ms under moderate concurrency (50–150 concurrent).
- Under 250 RPS steady with ~100 concurrent, expect P95 TTFT ~220–300ms. Burst to 800 RPS will push to ~350–500ms unless we: are (a) pre-warm scaled pools ahead of burst windows, or (b) fall back to a quantized 4/8-bit smaller model (~3B) for first-chunk only, then stream full-quality tokens once warmed.

Streaming transport & chunk cadence
- WebSocket recommended for mobile due to reconnection/backpressure+per-chunk ACKs; SSE ok for web only.
- Chunk sizing: recommend token-based gating with a soft target of 220–280 tokens per chunk or a hybrid: emit early partial chunk after 120–160 tokens if latency budget allows (gives visible content earlier). Also offer a heartbeat every 120ms for very long generations to keep UI responsive.

Operational controls & fallbacks
- Warm pool sizing: keep a small warm pool based on 60% of expected baseline concurrency and autoscale aggressively during forecasted bursts.
- Fallback policy: first-chunk served from quantized model variant when queue depth > threshold (e.g., > 75% utilization) and then failover to full model for subsequent tokens. Automated A/B rollback and telemetry hooks to measure quality drop.
- Telemetry: capture TTFT by route and by model variant; add an error budget alarm at 10% of requests >300ms.

Attachments: I’m attaching a quick estimate PDF that shows latency curves for 7B/13B on A100 and quantized variants.
